title: Gabber roots construct an integral idempotent section factor
statement: Let A and B be commutative rings, B an etale A-algebra [def-weil-etale-morphism], and I an ideal of A contained in its Jacobson radical. Assume every monic polynomial X^n(X-1)+sum_{j=0}^n a_j X^j with n>=1 and all a_j in I has a root alpha in 1+I. Given an A-algebra map sigma:B->A/I, there is an idempotent e in B such that A->B[1/e] is integral, the induced structure map A/I->B[1/e]/IB[1/e] is bijective, and there is an A-algebra map rho:B[1/e]->A/I with rho(x/1)=sigma(x) for every x in B. This asserts the integral factor construction, not an isomorphism A->B[1/e].

source.place: Lemma Tag 09XI (lemma-characterize-henselian-pair, line 2553), implication (5)$\Rightarrow$(2) and its proof (paragraphs from 'Assume (5). We will show that (2) holds' to the end of the proof): the section gives $A'/IA'\cong A/I\times C$ (Algebra Lemmas 00U7 lemma-map-between-etale and 00U8 lemma-surjective-flat-finitely-presented); integral closure $B'$ of $A$ in $A'$ and Lemma Tag 09XH (lemma-helper-finite-type, line 2502); a finite subalgebra $B''$ and Lemma Tag 0EM0 (lemma-helper-finite, line 2290) give $f$ as in (b) with $f(b)=0$; the root $a\in1+I$ splits $A[T]/(f)$ and hence $B'$ and $A'$; Lemma Tag 0ELZ (lemma-check-isomorphism-zariski, line 2265) concludes

proof.text: Apply the finite section model to obtain a finite subalgebra D, b∈D, the compatible closed-fibre product Φ and the b-localization isomorphism. Apply the finite Gabber polynomial theorem to D and b, with first factor A/I.

Choose α∈1+I by the root hypothesis. Write f=(X-C(α))g. Reduction modulo I and regularity of the monic X-1 give g mod I = X^n, so g(α)∈1+I is a unit. Put u=g(α)⁻¹ and d=u g(b). Write g-C(g(α))=(X-C(α))r. Evaluation of f(b)=0 gives (b-α)g(b)=0; the identity d-1=u(b-α)r(b) proves d(d-1)=0 and bd=αd. Reducing g and u modulo I shows d mod ID=b mod ID, using n≥1 and idempotence of the latter.
Apply the proved finite idempotent factor transfer to d and the unit α. This gives integrality of A→B[1/e] and bijectivity of the quotient structure map, for e the image of d.

The inclusion sends d to an idempotent e. Since the first coordinate of Φ(d mod ID) is 1 and equals σ(e), we have σ(e)=1. Use IsLocalization.Away.liftAlgHom to extend σ to ρ and Away.lift_eq to verify ρ(x/1)=σ(x).

proof_origin.place: Tag 09XI, proof of (5) implies (2), steps regrouped via a finite section model; polynomial calculation and transfer written in Lean by H2, 2026-10-12.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_gabber_integral_section_factor
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] (I : Ideal A) (hI : I ≤ Ideal.jacobson ⊥)
    (hroots : ∀ (n : ℕ), 1 ≤ n → ∀ (a : Fin (n + 1) → A),
      (∀ j, a j ∈ I) → ∀ (f : A[X]), f.Monic →
        f = X ^ n * (X - 1) + ∑ j : Fin (n + 1), C (a j) * X ^ (j : ℕ) →
          ∃ α : A, α - 1 ∈ I ∧ f.IsRoot α)
    (B : Type v) [CommRing B] [Algebra A B] [Etale A B] (σ : B →ₐ[A] A ⧸ I) :
    ∃ e : B, IsIdempotentElem e ∧
      (algebraMap A (Localization.Away e)).IsIntegral ∧
      Function.Bijective
        (Ideal.quotientMap (Ideal.map (algebraMap A (Localization.Away e)) I)
          (algebraMap A (Localization.Away e)) Ideal.le_comap_map) ∧
      ∃ ρ : Localization.Away e →ₐ[A] A ⧸ I,
        ∀ x : B, ρ (algebraMap B (Localization.Away e) x) = σ x
